comment: Ownership map for the private Cloud overlay (backenly/backenly-cloud).
PUBLIC IS THE DEFAULT. A path listed here is one the private overlay is
ALLOWED to own; everything not listed belongs to the public product and the
overlay may never write it. Enforced by scripts/verify-overlay-boundary.ts,
which CI runs in --strict mode: ANY public file tracked under one of these
paths is a violation, with no exemptions available.
Ownership is whole-directory wherever a private subsystem can have a
directory of its own, so the overlay only ever ADDS files and never has to
overwrite one the public repository tracks. Two paths are deliberate
file-level exceptions, both because their directory is MIXED and claiming
the whole of it would take public product code with it:
prisma/seed-billing.ts                  billing seed data, no directory
app/api/projects/[id]/access/route.ts   team management under a route
family that is otherwise entirely
per-project product
There was a `transition` key here from Phase 4 to Phase 7, grandfathering
public files that still sat under a future-private path. It went 73 -> 14 ->
0 and Phase 8 removed it. The verifier still UNDERSTANDS transition config
and still refuses a grandfather entry whose file is gone; that guard is
exercised against a synthetic config in tests/unit/overlay-ownership-boundary.spec.ts
rather than against this file, so it survives the key's removal.
Every path below is also listed in .gitignore, so a composed Cloud checkout
reports no untracked overlay files. A unit test asserts that parity.
